title.narrative: Regional strengthening of multi sector needs and analysis and drought response (24AWX)

description.narrative:
Objective 1 Improving access to and quality of information on the impact of drought on the population and their humanitarian needs for informed, evidence-based policy- and decision- making at county and community levels
Objective 2 Provision of Remote Sensing and regional style analysis across the drought affected areas in the Horn of Africa Region (Kenya, Somalia, and Ethiopia).

activity-date.narrative:
"Regional: REACH aims to leverage its regional approach by providing deeper analysis of existing sources to feed into an overall regional analysis products highlighting the most affected areas across the entire Horn of Africa. One core activity will be more granular remote sensing analysis across all three countries. REACH will utilize higher resolution data sources, like the 10m resolution Sentinel-2 sensor for instance, to derive trends and illustrate patterns of environmental change at the Admin 2 level and below, where possible. To track deficits or surpluses in rainfall throughout the water cycle, a combination of approaches will be used examining not just rainfall patterns but also trends in surface and subsurface soil moisture as well as measures of vegetation health.
Kenya: Primary data collection activities will be expanded through this project, which will allow for area-specific information products and will contribute to regional analytical products. REACH will conduct an assessment on the impact of drought in Turkana and Marsabit counties, which are hard-hit by the drought and considered to be candidates to potentially deteriorate into IPC Phase 4 levels of food insecurity. This assessment will provide a multi-sectoral lens to the National Drought Management Authority’s (NDMA) food security findings, to encourage implementing actors to take an integrated approach to humanitarian activities to minimise the risk of excess mortality. The assessment will use a mixed-methods approach; both household survey and key informant interviews will be conducted and involve extensive collaboration with key stakeholders. Overall, by bringing together a regional lens, the remote sensing in conjunction with the household level piece in Kenya, will combine to contribute to an overall better understanding of criticality and needs across the Horn of Africa. For all analytical products, REACH will conduct a comprehensive secondary data review and triangulate findings with primary data to produce sectoral and or geographically specific products that identifies trends in humanitarian needs and impacts of the drought. "

recipient-country.narrative: Against the backdrop of an unprecedented drought, sharp price increases for commodities, reduced donor funding and a related slow humanitarian response across the region, vulnerable communities in the Arid lands in Kenya, South and Central Somalia, conflict- and drought-affected regions of Ethiopia are all facing potentially dire situations. REACH proposes a multi-pronged approach to fill information management gaps and enhance the response and prioritisation of humanitarian and government actors in all three drought affected countries. In Kenya REACH will conduct an assessment in Turkana and Marsabit counties, which are hard-hit by the drought and considered to be candidates to potentially deteriorate into IPC Phase 4 levels of food insecurity. REACH will provide a multi-sectoral lens to the National Drought Management Authority’s (NDMA) food security findings, to encourage implementing actors to take an integrated approach to humanitarian activities to minimise the risk of excess mortality. Under the proposed project’s second objective, REACH will strengthen the analysis and remote sensing capacity of its existing activities, to provide granular data culminating in an analysis output that highlights most vulnerable populations across all three countries.
